question: Can the rank-collapse and entropy-collapse regimes of randomly initialized deep softmax Transformers be derived within one quantitative signal-propagation theory, and can query/key variance together with residual strength predict which initializations will train?

key_findings.claim: The paper maps each attention row at random initialization to a correlated Random Energy Model and predicts a query/key-variance phase transition between uniform and localized attention.
key_findings.evidence: With query/key variance scaled so attention-logit variance grows as log sequence length, the infinite-width, infinite-sequence analysis gives a geometry-dependent critical beta. Below it, the inverse participation ratio tends to zero and attention averages tokens; above it, the inverse participation ratio stays nonzero and only O(1) keys effectively receive attention.

anchors.section: 3.1 Self-Attention and the Random Energy Model, Equations 7-9
Rank Collapse and Entropy Collapse discussion

key_findings.claim: In the model's asymptotic regime, neither side of the phase transition is independently trainable: small beta promotes rank collapse, whereas large beta produces entropy collapse that residual connections do not remove.
key_findings.evidence: For beta below the critical value, a bare attention layer sends average token cosine similarity to one; sufficiently strong residual connections preserve token diversity. For beta above the critical value, attention stays diverse across queries but each row is localized on an initialization-selected set of keys. The resulting prescription is small query/key variance plus a depth-dependent minimum self-attention residual strength.

anchors.section: Rank Collapse, Entropy Collapse, and Take-Home Message

key_findings.claim: The backward analysis creates a finite-training-timescale gap in the practical prescription: the recommended low-beta regime has vanishing query/key gradients at initialization in the same asymptotic limit.
key_findings.evidence: Result 2 makes the query/key gradient norm depend on participation ratios that vanish for low beta, even when input tokens have not rank-collapsed. The paper resolves the apparent paradox qualitatively by arguing that residual-stream gradients update embeddings after the first backward pass and break the simplex geometry, but it does not derive how large or how fast the recovered query/key gradients become at finite width and sequence length.

anchors.section: 3.3 The Backward Pass, Result 2 and Vanishing Gradients

key_findings.claim: Iterating two scalar order parameters through attention, residual, LayerNorm, and MLP updates yields architecture-specific trainability diagrams, but the reduction depends on permutation-symmetric simplex geometry.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithms 1-3 update average token norm q and overlap p for post-norm, pre-norm, and gain-controlled blocks. This compression is justified for non-causal, infinitely long sequences whose token geometry remains approximately simplex-like; the autoregressive experiment shows it is inaccurate for early positions and only becomes predictive for late tokens.

anchors.section: 4 Full Transformer Block Analysis and Algorithm 1

key_findings.claim: The BERT-style TinyStories experiments qualitatively separate trainable, rank-collapse, and entropy-collapse initializations in the directions predicted by the phase diagram.
key_findings.evidence: For low beta, the measured token-cosine trajectories across 60 layers track the theoretical curves as residual strength varies; the 60-layer models with weak residuals fail while stronger-residual models train. Separate 12-layer high-beta models fail despite being shallow enough to avoid rank collapse, and one-layer beta sweeps show low attention entropy and poor loss at high beta.

key_findings.claim: The paper's strongest architectural follow-up is gain-controlled attention, which centers the value aggregation and empirically slows rank collapse, but its training evidence is explicitly preliminary.
key_findings.evidence: Subtracting the sequence mean from attention values removes the shared p contribution from the attention update. The resulting theory avoids rank collapse, and a 30-layer single-head post-norm BERT-style model trains on TinyStories where the vanilla counterpart fails. The authors state that experiments at scale are outside the paper's scope.

anchors.section: C.1 Training Gain-Controlled Transformers on TinyStories

key_findings.claim: The advertised asymptotic exactness is narrower than a fully rigorous end-to-end theorem because one cross-row attention term and the finite-size regime are handled approximately.
key_findings.evidence: The derivation of the cross-overlap Yp explicitly assumes a self-averaging term, uses an approximation, and supplements it with beta-to-zero and beta-to-infinity intuition before declaring the term sub-leading. The finite-size section labels its correction argument non-rigorous and predicts a broad non-Gaussian crossover beginning at half the asymptotic critical beta.

anchors.section: Definition of beta_c and Finite-Size Effects

key_findings.claim: The experiment specification contains a concrete reproducibility contradiction for Figure 2.
key_findings.evidence: The Figure 2 caption states that the single-layer simulation uses embedding dimension d=512 and sequence length T=1024, whereas Appendix A.2 states d=600 for the same T=1024 comparison. The text provides no reconciliation or separate run label.

key_findings.claim: The phrase 'entropy collapse' joins two related but not yet proven-identical phenomena: localization at random initialization and low entropy that emerges during unstable training.
key_findings.evidence: The theory diagnoses the high-beta initialized attention matrix through a nonzero inverse participation ratio, while the motivating prior work tracked entropy falling during training. The paper's one-layer intervention connects high-beta initialization to poor training, and its appendix shows that lowering the learning rate partially mitigates the problem, but it does not establish that normal-initialization training-induced collapse follows the same Random Energy Model transition.

anchors.section: C.3 Entropy Collapse Can Be Mitigated by Low Learning Rate

key_findings.claim: The broad claim of being the first full or unified Transformer signal-propagation theory must be narrowed against a direct 2024 predecessor not discussed in the paper.
key_findings.evidence: The target related-work section contrasts primarily with uniform-attention and annealed-softmax analyses and later claims a full theory. Transformers Get Stable, accepted at ICML 2024, had already presented end-to-end forward/backward moment propagation through Transformer components, initialization guidance for high query/key values, rank-collapse mitigation, and DeepScaleLM experiments up to 1,000 layers. The target remains differentiated by its long-sequence correlated-softmax Random Energy Model and exact critical constants within that asymptotic model.

method.core_idea: Treat correlated random attention logits as a Random Energy Model, derive a localization transition in the infinite-sequence limit, and compose that attention update with residual, normalization, and MLP signal-propagation maps.
method.mechanism: The method tracks the average squared token norm q and pairwise overlap p. A replica calculation gives the participation ratio of one softmax row as a function of the query/key scale beta and the current token geometry; the attention update maps q and p differently below and above the critical beta. Residual branches, LayerNorm, and two-layer MLP covariance maps are then applied in block order. Iteration over depth yields token-cosine trajectories and a two-dimensional trainability diagram over beta and self-attention residual strength. A separate Jacobian calculation relates query/key gradient norm to second- and third-order participation ratios.
assumptions: Embedding width and non-causal sequence length tend to infinity, with query/key variance scaled so attention-logit variance is proportional to log sequence length.
Token representations are permutation-symmetric and approximately simplex-like, so their geometry is captured by a common norm q and common off-diagonal overlap p.
Query, key, and value matrices are independent zero-mean Gaussian initializations; the simplified LayerNorm omits its affine transformation.
Fluctuations around the average overlap are sub-leading, and the cross-row attention overlap Yp is sub-leading under the self-averaging approximation in Appendix B.2.2.
The loss-dependent prefactor in the query/key gradient bound scales as O(1/T), as assumed and numerically checked in the gradient experiment.
Finite width, finite sequence length, positional structure, multi-head coupling, and causal masks do not invalidate the qualitative phase classification in the evaluated regime.
Residual-stream parameter updates break the simplex geometry soon enough to restore useful query/key learning in the low-beta regime after the first backward pass.
Training success is sufficiently predicted by initialization-time signal statistics despite optimizer, data, and feature-learning dynamics outside the theory.

techniques.role: Maps a row of Gaussian-correlated softmax logits to a Random Energy Model in order to calculate its localization transition.
Measures the effective number of attended keys and distinguishes spread attention from entropy-localized attention.
Compresses the token covariance geometry into q and p and iterates them through Transformer blocks.
Sweeps query/key scale and self-attention skip strength to partition initializations into rank-collapse, entropy-collapse, and trainable regions.
Expresses initial query/key gradient norm using token geometry and higher-order participation ratios.
Removes the sequence-mean value component so attention no longer injects the common overlap term that drives rank collapse.

evaluations.setting: One random self-attention layer with sequence length T=1024 over a sweep of beta and input token cosine similarity.
evaluations.metric: Average output token cosine similarity and phase-boundary agreement.
evaluations.result: Simulation qualitatively reproduces the theoretical transition, with deviations near the critical region attributed to finite-size effects; the reported dimension is internally inconsistent, d=512 in the caption and d=600 in Appendix A.2.
evaluations.baseline: The infinite-width, infinite-sequence Result 1 phase diagram.

evaluations.setting: Post-norm BERT-style masked-language models on TinyStories with 60 layers in the low-beta regime and 12 layers in the high-beta regime; the detailed recipe uses six heads, d=600, batch size 64, and one epoch.
evaluations.metric: Layerwise average token cosine similarity and test-loss learning curves.
evaluations.result: Empirical cosine trajectories track the q,p iteration; strong residual settings train, weak-residual low-beta settings fail through rank collapse, and high-beta settings fail through low-entropy attention despite the shallower depth.
evaluations.baseline: Vanilla BERT initialization across two residual strengths from each predicted phase.

evaluations.setting: Single-layer, single-head BERT-style masked-language model on TinyStories with d=768 and a beta sweep.
evaluations.metric: Average attention-row Shannon entropy and test loss during one epoch.
evaluations.result: Low-beta attention can diversify during training and lowers loss, whereas high-beta attention remains concentrated and trains poorly; a lower learning rate partially mitigates the latter in Appendix C.3.
evaluations.baseline: Identical architecture and optimizer recipe with beta varied from below to above the predicted critical value.

evaluations.setting: Random self-attention gradient experiment over T in {2048, 4096, 8192} and d in {256, 512, 1024}.
evaluations.metric: Scaled Frobenius norm of the query-weight gradient as a function of beta.
evaluations.result: The rescaled curves collapse and show strongly suppressed gradients in the low-beta range, with the finite-size crossover beginning near half the asymptotic critical beta.

evaluations.setting: Thirty-layer, single-head, post-norm BERT-style TinyStories training with d=480, unit residual coefficients, and half an epoch.
evaluations.metric: Training loss under vanilla versus gain-controlled attention.
evaluations.result: The gain-controlled model trains in a regime where the vanilla 30-layer model fails; the experiment is preliminary and not repeated at production scale or across domains.
evaluations.baseline: Vanilla softmax attention with the same architecture and training recipe.

evaluations.setting: Fifty-layer post-norm autoregressive Transformer with d=720 on approximately 200-token sequences, averaged over ten initializations and ten sequences.
evaluations.metric: Layerwise token cosine similarity for early, full-sequence, and late token subsets.
evaluations.result: The two-parameter theory misses early-token dynamics, partially matches whole-sequence averages, and tracks the last 50 tokens where the simplex geometry is better established.
evaluations.baseline: The non-causal q,p propagation theory applied without an explicit causal-position state.

limitations: Author-stated: the critical transition is asymptotic; for finite sequences, non-Gaussian fluctuations begin near beta_c/2 and smear the transition before beta_c.
Author-stated: the two-parameter simplex description is inadequate for early causal positions and only approximates sufficiently late tokens.
Author-stated: gain-controlled-attention experiments at scale are outside scope, and the reported evidence is a 30-layer TinyStories pilot.
Author-stated: an infinitely deep non-collapsing fixed point with tanh requires placing the MLP in a chaotic regime associated with exploding gradients and unstable training.

Reviewer-identified: the proof of the cross-row attention overlap uses an explicit self-averaging approximation, so the presented derivation does not fully justify an unqualified 'asymptotically exact' claim.

Reviewer-identified: the empirical training evidence is concentrated on small BERT-style TinyStories runs, often one head or one epoch, and does not test modern decoder-only LLMs, multiple corpora, or billion-parameter scale.

Reviewer-identified: initialization-time signal propagation is necessary but not a guarantee of smooth optimization, generalization, or robustness under different optimizers and learning-rate schedules.
Reviewer-identified: the low-beta gradient paradox is resolved qualitatively through residual-stream updates but lacks a finite-time theory of gradient recovery.
Reviewer-identified: Figure 2's embedding dimension is reported inconsistently as 512 and 600.
Reviewer-identified: the theoretical initialization-localization transition is not proven to be identical to entropy collapse that emerges during ordinary training.
failure_modes: A finite-sequence model can lie in the broad beta_c/2-to-beta_c crossover where the asymptotic phase label gives a poor quantitative prediction.
Causal early-token geometry, padding masks, heterogeneous positions, or structured data can require more than the two averaged covariance parameters q and p.
Very small beta can keep query/key learning too weak for too long even when residuals prevent forward rank collapse.
Large beta can localize attention on initialization-specific keys; residual paths preserve token state but do not de-localize the attention rows.
An initialization can preserve average cosine diversity while still losing task-relevant subspaces, suffering head-specific collapse, or having unstable gradient singular values.
Gain-controlled value centering can remove a useful global mean feature or interact poorly with masks and causal prefix statistics.
A learning-rate or optimizer change can rescue or break a phase-diagram setting, exposing the limits of an initialization-only trainability claim.
The replica/self-averaging calculation can fail outside Gaussian, independent-weight, permutation-symmetric, or long-sequence regimes.
reusable_insights: Track both representation rank and attention-row localization: high token diversity does not imply healthy attention entropy, and high entropy does not ensure useful representation diversity.
Initialization guidance should couple query/key scale to sequence length and residual scale to depth rather than tune either in isolation.
A trainability proxy should report its finite-size uncertainty band around a phase boundary instead of returning a hard asymptotic label.
Separate exact asymptotic claims, finite-size approximations, and empirical optimizer effects in both theory and UI presentation.
Position-stratified diagnostics are essential for causal Transformers because averages over a whole sequence can hide early-versus-late geometric regimes.
Centering or projecting out the uniform attention mode is a reusable intervention shared by value-centering and spectral-gap-removal approaches.
Initialization-time gradient diagnostics should be followed through the first several optimizer steps to test whether residual updates actually escape the degenerate geometry.
open_questions: Can the Random Energy Model calculation be extended rigorously to finite T with calibrated error bars through the non-Gaussian crossover?
What minimal position-dependent state replaces q and p for causal attention while remaining computationally tractable?
How quickly do query/key gradients recover after residual-stream updates in the low-beta regime, and how does that timescale scale with width, context length, depth, and learning rate?
Do the predicted beta and residual thresholds transfer to multi-head decoder-only LLMs trained at billion-parameter and long-context scale?
Is training-induced entropy collapse under standard initialization governed by the same localization transition as high-beta collapse at initialization?
Can gain-controlled attention preserve useful global-token information while removing only the pathological uniform spectral mode?
How do Random Energy Model localization, attention-matrix spectral gaps, and Jacobian singular-value dynamics fit into one finite-size theory?
Does a phase-diagram initialization still improve final loss after equalizing optimizer tuning and compute against DeepScaleLM, DeepNorm, sigma-Reparam, and spectral-gap removal?

competitive_landscape.title: DeepNet: Scaling Transformers to 1,000 Layers
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct practical initialization and residual-scaling predecessor
competitive_landscape.difference: DeepNet derives DeepNorm residual and initialization scalings from bounded model updates and demonstrates extremely deep encoder-decoder training. The target instead predicts rank-versus-entropy regimes from token geometry and query/key localization, but validates at much smaller scale.

competitive_landscape.title: Signal Propagation in Transformers: Theoretical Perspectives and the Role of Rank Collapse
competitive_landscape.difference: Noci et al. show that rank-collapsed token representations cause vanishing query/key gradients and prescribe depth-dependent residual scaling, effectively analyzing near-uniform attention. The target recovers that low-beta regime and adds an explicit high-beta localization transition and quantitative critical query/key scale.

competitive_landscape.title: Stabilizing Transformer Training by Preventing Attention Entropy Collapse
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct entropy-collapse predecessor and intervention baseline
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhai et al. observe entropy collapse during training across vision, speech, translation, and language tasks, bound entropy using logit spectral norms, and propose sigma-Reparam. The target gives an initialization-time long-sequence localization threshold for standard softmax but tests fewer domains and does not prove the two collapse processes are identical.

competitive_landscape.title: Geometric Dynamics of Signal Propagation Predict Trainability of Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Cowsik et al. evolve permutation-symmetric token geometry through attention and nonlinear MLPs, deriving forward and backward Lyapunov exponents whose joint criticality predicts test loss. Their annealed softmax treatment captures order-chaos behavior but not the target's large-deviation high-beta entropy-localization phase.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers Get Stable: An End-to-End Signal Propagation Theory for Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: omitted direct unified-theory and initialization competitor
competitive_landscape.difference: Kedia et al. already provide forward/backward moment equations for full Transformer components, diagnose high query/key instability and rank collapse, and introduce DeepScaleLM with experiments up to 1,000 layers across encoder, decoder, vision, and speech settings. The target's narrower differentiation is an asymptotic correlated-softmax calculation with a critical beta and joint rank/entropy phase diagram.

competitive_landscape.title: Mind the Gap: a Spectral Analysis of Rank Collapse and Signal Propagation in Attention Layers
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct spectral account and centering intervention
competitive_landscape.difference: Nait Saada et al. identify softmax attention's leading spectral outlier as the cause of rank collapse in width and remove it to slow rank and gradient pathologies, including tests with LayerNorm and skips. The target instead removes the mean value contribution in its gain-controlled variant and derives a query/key localization phase transition; the two approaches project out closely related uniform modes from different sides of attention.

competitive_landscape.title: Subcritical Signal Propagation at Initialization in Normalization-Free Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Alekseev tracks averaged partial Jacobian norms and activation recurrences in bidirectional, permutation-symmetric normalization-free Transformers, explaining power-law versus stretched-exponential depth behavior in Dynamic Tanh and Dynamic erf models. It extends the initialization theory toward normalization-free architectures, whereas the target focuses on softmax localization and LayerNorm placement.

competitive_landscape.title: Sinkhorn doubly stochastic attention rank decay analysis
competitive_landscape.difference: Lapenna et al. study Sinkhorn-normalized doubly stochastic attention, showing improved rank preservation but still doubly exponential rank-one decay without skips. This tests an entropy-regularized alternative to standard softmax rather than selecting a safe beta within standard attention.

competitive_landscape.title: Rank, Head-Channel Non-Identifiability, and Symmetry Breaking: A Precise Analysis of Representational Collapse in Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: subsequent conceptual refinement of collapse taxonomy
competitive_landscape.difference: Cirrincione distinguishes rank collapse in depth and width from head-channel non-identifiability and argues that residual connections generically obstruct rank collapse in realistic Transformers while LayerNorm is affine-rank-neutral. The target supplies quantitative residual thresholds and an entropy-localization regime but does not address head identifiability or this broader symmetry taxonomy.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims an asymptotically exact, down-to-the-constant signal-propagation theory for complete deep Transformer blocks that unifies rank collapse and entropy collapse and yields practical initialization trainability diagrams.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Its distinctive technical contribution is the correlated Random Energy Model treatment of standard softmax at log-sequence-scaled query/key variance, producing a geometry-dependent critical beta, inverse-participation-ratio formulas, a residual-strength boundary, and blockwise q,p update algorithms tested on BERT-style models.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the long-sequence large-deviation calculation and joint phase diagram, not the first unified or end-to-end Transformer signal-propagation theory: Cowsik et al. and especially Kedia et al. already covered full-block forward/backward propagation and initialization guidance. The target's exactness and training-guarantee language should also be qualified because the cross-row term uses self-averaging, finite-size corrections are non-rigorous, the low-beta gradient recovery is qualitative, and training tests are narrow.

reviewer_notes: Read all 27 cached pages, including the main derivations, all three block algorithms, experiment appendices, finite-size argument, gain-controlled pilot, and causal-position study. The source bytes and hashes match the fulltext index entry exactly. Nine direct primary records were checked on arXiv on 2026-08-23, including three subsequent 2026 refinements; the closest omitted predecessor is arXiv:2403.09635. Explicit contradictions retained in this reading are the d=512 versus d=600 Figure 2 specification, the self-averaging/non-rigorous steps beneath unqualified exactness language, the initialization-versus-training meanings of entropy collapse, and the unsupported breadth of a training guarantee. This is a primary full-text pass, not an independent second-review promotion.
